It includes newspapers, radio, cinema, television etc. These media fill minds of people and influence the culture by providing news, recreation, education etc.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"What is the family formed between Parvej and Mita be called? Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"The family formed between Parvej and Mita is a single and neo-local family.
Based on size, family can be of three types – single or nuclear family, joint family, and extended family. The family where husband, wife and their unmarried children live together is known as single or nuclear family. Again, family-based on dwelling place of husband and wife after marriage can be of three types – patrilocal, matrilocal and neo-local. The married couple does not live either with the husband’s or the wife’s paternal house, rather they live in a new place is known as neo-local family.
In the stem, Parvej got acquainted with Mita while studying at the university. After completion of study, they got married. As their parents did not accept their relationship, they started living in a separate house. They have two children. As their family comprises of husband, wife and unmarried children, it is a single or nuclear family. Again, due to living in a separate house after marriage, their family is a neo-local family. So, the family of Parvej and Mita is a single and neo-local family.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"“The role of parents is key to develop Parvej and Mita’s children as social being” – Analyze. Learning Outcomes-2 & 9 [B.B. 2020]","marks":4,"answer":"The role of parents is the key to develop Parvej and Mita’s children as social beings.
A child becomes a social being through the process of socialization. And, family is the most important medium of socialization. The space of socialization becomes ready within the family prior to the birth of a child. Naturally, all the good and bad aspects of family life influence children’s behaviour. The social, moral and civic sense are introduced within the family.
In the stem, Parvej and Mita have two children. As their family is neo-local, the influence of Parvej and Mita will be greater on the socialization process of their children. The dear and near persons to a child are its parents. Parents help to form the eating habit and language learning ability of the children. Their conduct and values influence the socialization process. As Parvej and Mita both are service holders and their family do not have any other members or relatives, they will have a greater contribution to the development of their children as social beings. They must find time for their children from their busy schedule. They should spend time with their children more often. Their children should not be in hands on domestic servant of which could disrupt their socialization process.
In the end, it can be said that the parents influence children as only family members in a single family. So, the role of parents is key to develop Parvej and Mita’s children as social beings.
---","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Mili lives in an urban nuclear family with busy working parents. Her socialization is heavily influenced by mass media (TV, video games) and limited family interaction. She learns independently but may lack direct social engagement and traditional values.

There are two types of families based on authority. Such as- patriarchal and matriarchal. A family where the overall power and authority of the family rests on the male members of the family, it is called a patriarchal family. A family where the overall power and authority of the family rests on the female members of the family, it is called a matriarchal family. Families of Garos and Khasias, minority ethnic communities of Bangladesh, have matriarchal families.
In Incident 1 of the stem, we can see that Hira goes to visit his friend Martin’s house. There he sees that Martin’s mother holds all the authority over the family. Learning Outcomes-2 & 11","marks":4,"answer":"The most important component of socialization in case of a healthy socialization for children like Abir is social life.
Social life plays an important role in the healthy socialization of an individual. People’s social lives are mainly controlled by some behaviour. Social life is the sum of the behaviour of the society in which an individual lives. People participate in many activities of the society. People try to adapt by dealing with the behaviour associated with these actions. In such situations, people often imitate behaviour of others. Meaning, people master many things such as language, pronunciation, manner of speaking etc. from the tendency to imitate. In case of Abir in the stem, this can be observed.
In the stem, Abir is a 7 years old child. As both his parents are busy with their jobs, they cannot give him sufficient time. This is why, Abir mixes with the maid’s son and is busy fighting and playing with him. The influence of the maid’s son is noticeable in his way of talking, behaviour and activities. Meaning, Abir is imitating the behaviour and activities of the maid’s son. This happens mainly due to the influence of social life.
If Abir’s parents could give him enough time, took him to the different places and he could involve into many social activities like meeting the neighbour’s children, attending many occasions observed by the society could have shaped his socialization process into a better one. Among the social institutions, the smallest institution is family. And the modern form of this institution is single or nuclear family. Although the family arrangement of Bangladesh is traditionally joint family based, majority of the family arrangement is being built based on single or nuclear family like the western world.
In the stem it can be observed that, Mita’s family consists of her parents and herself and they live in the city. The family where husband, wife and their unmarried children live together is called a single or nuclear family. In this case, the family Mita lives in is indicating a single or nuclear family through its characteristics. Nuclear families are being formed by breakdown of joint families by the direct impact of urbanization and industrialization, increase of literacy rate, change in values, extreme development of technology and overall globalization. In a nuclear family, there is simplicity of a well-to-do life, arrangement to fulfil the basic demands of the fundamental demands of the few family members and the possibility of a hassle-free lifestyle. Learning Outcomes-2 & 10 [D.B. 2019]","marks":4,"answer":"The socialization process of Ria and Mita are different due to their contrasting living environments—urban vs. rural—and the resulting differences in family structure, daily activities, and social exposures.
Mita lives in an urban nuclear family. Her socialization is influenced by modern facilities like television and video games, structured extracurricular activities, and limited family members. Her interactions are more formal and scheduled, often centered around technology and organized programs.
Ria lives in a rural joint family. Her socialization is deeply rooted in traditional family values, multi-generational interactions, and community engagement. She learns through direct participation in household chores, helping neighbors, and informal interactions within a close-knit community.
These differences lead to variations in their values, social skills, and worldviews. Mita may develop more individualistic and tech-savvy traits, while Ria may embody collectivist values, empathy, and practical life skills. Thus, their socialization processes are inherently different in nature.

Learning Outcomes-2 & 4","marks":4,"answer":"In context-2, although Rakhal’s father wants to protect the blood bond and purity, Rakhal wants to prevent social injustices – the statement is correct.
As described in context-2, when Rakhal Bandhopadhhay wants to get married to Sabita Das, his father does not agree to the marriage. His father wishes Rakhal to marry a girl whose caste is equal to theirs. This type of families, based on selection of bride or groom, exist extensively in the Hindu society. In this type of a family, the blood bond and purity must be protected through marriage within the same caste. However, there are some families who want to prevent social injustice by marrying outside their caste.
On the basis of selection of bride or groom, two types of families can be seen in the Hindu society. Such as, exogenous and endogamous family. When a person marries outside his own caste, it is called an exogenous family. This kind of family is of two types. When a bridegroom of higher caste marries a bride of lower caste, it is called an anulome marriage based family. On the other hand, when a bridegroom of lower caste marries a bride of higher caste, it is called a proilome marriage based family. The root cause of such type of marriage is to prevent social injustice. When a person marries within his caste it is called an endogamous family. This type of endogamous marriages are more common in Hindu society. To protect the so-called blood bond and to keep its purity intact is the only reason behind this type of marriage.
In conclusion, it can be said that in context-2 although his father’s intention was to protect blood bonds and keeping its purity intact through marriage to someone of the same caste, Rakhal intended to prevent social injustice by marrying someone outside his own caste.","image":null,"image_url":null}]

In a family where the overall power and authority is in the hands of the mother, that family is called a matrilineal family. In a matriarchal or matrilineal family, children get family status and property inheritance through mother. In this family system, the policy of a matrilocal family is followed. In this type of family, after the marriage the groom lives with his in-laws instead of living in his own house.
In the stem, we can see that in case of Tamama’s friend’s marriage, the mother plays the key role. After the marriage, the groom lives in her friend’s mother’s house and when the mother dies, her friend will inherit all the property. Here, a matriarchal or matrilineal family has been indicated very clearly. In such a family, the family name and inheritance of property comes down from the mother to the daughter. This kind of family system exists among the minority ethnic groups of Bangladesh such as Garo and Khasia. In such a type of family, the mother is the authoritative figure. So, it can be said that Tamama’s friend is a member of a matriarchal family.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"In the present changed situation, has the customary practice seen in her friend’s wedding become extinct? Give logic in support of your answer. Learning Outcomes-2 & 4","marks":4,"answer":"No, in the present changed situation the customary practice of the groom living in the in-laws house or matrilocal family has not become extinct but instead has decreased.
Based on the dwelling place of the husband and wife after marriage, the types of families that can be seen are patrilocal, matrilocal and neo-local. If the newly married couple live in the wife’s mother’s house, it is called matrilocal family and if the couple lives in the husband’s father’s house, it is called a patrilocal family. However, if the newly married couple do not live either in the wife’s or husband’s father’s house, but live in a separate house, it is called a neo-local family. At present, alongside patrilocal and matrilocal families, the number of neo-local families is also increasing.
In the stem we can see that, the mother played the key role in Tamama’s friend’s wedding and after the wedding, the husband is living in the wife’s mother’s house. Here according to the marriage custom, a matrilocal family has been indicated. In the present changed situation, matrilocal families have not become extinction however, some changes can be observed. Matrilocal families can be in among the Garo and Khasia in Bangladesh. Lately, a few educated Garo couples live in the husband’s father’s house. That is, they have a patriarchal attitude. Although the property in the family belongs to the wife, the responsibility of managing them is the husband’s. Again, in the Khasia’ matriarchal social system, although there is a custom of the husband living in the wife’s house, after the birth of a child, the husband can take the wife to his own home. Beside, at present, educated service holder husband and wife are building up neo-local families.
From the discussion above, it can be said that the present changed situation has not made the matrilocal family system like Tamama’s friend’s family extinct but has increased the number of patrilocal and neo-local families.
